items.title: Key identity is not bound to value identity or an authorization subject
items.statement: Both keys carry project and run or assignment identity, but the value schemas only require non-empty strings. They do not require key components to equal value fields, identify a tenant or actor, or prove that the writer is authorized for the project. A misplaced or adversarially constructed value can therefore validate under the wrong key and authority context.
items.impact: Cross-project substitution, confused-deputy writes, and resume of the wrong run or wave remain schema-valid.
items.builder_discretion: Define key/value equality checks and an explicit authenticated project authority binding outside free-form identifiers.

items.title: Mutable run and wave rows have no concurrency token, lease, or idempotency key
items.statement: The contracts support resume, retry, status mutation, receipts, and parent writeback, yet expose no revision, compare-and-swap token, lease owner/expiry, attempt identity, or idempotency key. Concurrent resume, retry, cancellation, supersession, and parent writeback can race, lose updates, or publish duplicate completions.
items.impact: A stale worker can overwrite a newer state or complete the same assignment more than once without violating either schema.
items.builder_discretion: Choose a monotonic revision/CAS and durable attempt-idempotency model; its observable conflict behavior must be normative.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Resume by exact run id; stale currentness, unsupported contract mode, or missing receipts keep PlanCompile disabled.",
"replay_behavior": "Replay restores assignment state and parent-only write obligations without dispatching product work.",

items.title: PlanCompile status is not coupled to blockers, receipts, currentness, or stage
items.statement: The schema independently validates status, current_stage, currentness_status, blockers, and receipts. It has no conditional invariants or transition table, so ready_for_bootstrap_validation can coexist with stale currentness, arbitrary stage, blockers, or empty receipts, and blocked can carry no blocker at all.
items.impact: Implementation-readiness and disabled-state consumers can project a false runnable or blocked state from a schema-valid row.
items.builder_discretion: Specify permitted transitions and cross-field predicates, including the exact receipt and currentness oracle for every state.

items.title: Opaque objects and unbounded collections defeat validation, redaction, and scale guarantees
items.statement: cursor, currentness_status, source_hashes, cancellation, and supersession are unconstrained objects, while multiple arrays have neither size bounds nor string bounds. These surfaces admit arbitrary nesting, oversized values, secret-bearing content, ambiguous semantics, and inputs for which no deterministic acceptance oracle exists.
items.impact: Malformed or hostile rows can exhaust decoding/storage resources, evade no-secret intent, and produce consumer-specific interpretations.
items.builder_discretion: Replace opaque objects with closed versioned schemas and establish byte, item-count, nesting, and string-length limits.

items.title: Cancellation and supersession have no destructive-action or rollback contract
items.statement: cancelled and superseded are valid states, but the corresponding objects are optional and completely open. No actor, authorization proof, reason, timestamp, target/replacement id, acknowledgement, rollback boundary, child-wave propagation, or terminality rule is required.
items.impact: Irreversible state changes can be unaudited, orphan child work, or be resumed inconsistently after partial cancellation or supersession.
items.builder_discretion: Define authenticated command receipts, propagation order, idempotency, and explicit recovery semantics for both actions.

items.title: Declared legacy import outcome is not representable or enforceable
items.statement: The migration prose says old draft fields become non-buildable lineage, but the schema has no lineage provenance, import version, source format, quarantine reason, or dedicated non-buildable state. A migration implementation therefore cannot prove the promised disposition from the stored value.
items.impact: Legacy data can be mistaken for native current data or become buildable through consumer-specific inference.
items.builder_discretion: Define a closed lineage envelope and a machine-checkable non-buildable state with migration-version evidence.

evidence.exact_quote: "migration": "No runtime PlanCompile rows are accepted without schema_version and contract_mode; old draft fields are imported only as non-buildable lineage.",

items.title: Receipt and evidence references carry no integrity, type, or resolution state
items.statement: Run receipts, wave assignment/completion receipts, and durable evidence are plain strings. The contracts do not bind a digest, media/schema type, issuer, creation time, verification result, or resolvability state, and expose no structured last-error information when verification fails.
items.impact: Missing, substituted, stale, or wrong-type evidence can be indistinguishable from valid evidence, undermining readiness and support diagnosis.
items.builder_discretion: Use typed content-addressed refs plus explicit verification and failure states.

items.title: Wave read/write boundary sets have no set algebra or canonical resource grammar
items.statement: read_set, write_set, forbidden_writes, and parent_only_writes are unrestricted string arrays. Empty and duplicate sets validate; the same target can appear in mutually conflicting sets; no resource grammar, containment rule, precedence, normalization, or evaluation algorithm is specified. This directly contradicts the migration claim that boundaries determine runtime validity.
items.impact: A worker or validator can interpret conflicting authority differently, permitting forbidden writes or rejecting legitimate work.
items.builder_discretion: Define canonical resource identifiers, non-empty requirements, disjointness/containment predicates, and deny-first conflict semantics.

evidence.exact_quote: "migration": "Wave rows without read/write/forbidden boundaries are invalid for runtime bootstrap and remain source-lineage only.",

items.title: Wave retry and resume are not a bounded, observable state machine
items.statement: result_status is an enum, retry_route is an arbitrary non-empty string, and resume_ref is nullable, but no legal transitions, attempt counter, retry budget, backoff, failure class, checkpoint semantics, timeout, or terminal-state rule is defined. The schema also has no wave timestamps.
items.impact: Partial failures can loop forever, restart from an unsafe point, or diverge between parent and worker without diagnosable evidence.
items.builder_discretion: Define the transition graph, durable attempt identity, retry budget, failure taxonomy, and checkpoint validity rules.

items.title: Completion and parent-writeback fields can contradict result status
items.statement: completion_receipt is nullable for every state and parent_writeback_required is an unconstrained boolean. The schema allows completed with no completion receipt, pending with a completion receipt, completed with required writeback false despite parent-only writes, or failed with arbitrary completion evidence.
items.impact: The parent can accept incomplete work, omit a mandatory merge, or repeat an already applied writeback.
items.builder_discretion: Couple result status, completion receipt verification, parent-only writes, and writeback acknowledgement with conditional schema and transactional semantics.

items.title: Retention and compaction lack a privacy and deletion lifecycle
items.statement: Retention is described only through dependent receipts/evidence and supersession. There is no time bound, deletion trigger, tombstone, legal-hold rule, user/project deletion propagation, compaction proof, or treatment of refs after target data expires.
items.impact: Historical rows and potentially sensitive references may persist indefinitely or be deleted while still required, with no auditable outcome.
items.builder_discretion: Define retention classes, deletion and hold precedence, reference expiry behavior, and a verifiable compaction receipt.

evidence.exact_quote: "retention_compaction": "Retain through all child receipts and audit evidence; superseded runs are historical but not resumable unless currentness says so.",
"retention_compaction": "Retain until the parent PlanCompileRun is superseded and all evidence refs are preserved.",

items.title: Disabled-state projection has no stable reason model for truthful, accessible, localized UI
items.statement: The Planning Wizard is an explicit consumer, but blockers are untyped free-form strings and currentness is an opaque object. There are no stable reason codes, severity/priority, remediation affordance, localization parameters, or announcement semantics. Different consumers can display contradictory or inaccessible disabled-state explanations.
items.impact: Users may see an enabled action that cannot proceed, an unexplained disabled action, untranslated internal text, or state changes that assistive technology cannot interpret consistently.
items.builder_discretion: Store stable machine reason codes and structured parameters; keep localized display text and accessibility behavior in the UI contract.

items.title: Lifecycle, migration, compaction, security, and support callers are absent from consumer ownership
items.statement: The registry names resume/UI/readiness and parent/validator/projector consumers, while the same contracts require migration, retention/compaction, evidence preservation, redaction, cancellation, and supersession behavior. No consumer is assigned to execute or verify those obligations, leaving ownership and invocation seams unresolved.
items.impact: Normative lifecycle duties can remain unimplemented because every listed consumer can plausibly treat them as someone else's responsibility.
items.builder_discretion: Assign explicit consumer/owner identities for migration, compaction, evidence verification, security review, and support diagnostics.

items.title: External reference loss has no offline or degraded-resolution state
items.statement: Sensitive/runtime material is intentionally external-ref-only, and receipts/evidence are refs, but neither schema records whether a target is cached, unavailable, denied, expired, corrupt, or last verified. Replay and GUI consumers therefore cannot distinguish transient network or storage loss from invalid evidence or policy denial.
items.impact: Offline operation may incorrectly disable, resume, or invalidate work and provide no deterministic recovery path after connectivity returns.
items.builder_discretion: Define resolution states, last-known verification metadata, safe offline behavior, and recovery/revalidation ordering.

evidence.exact_quote: "redaction_no_secret_rule": "Stores ids, refs, hashes, stages, and enum status only; provider/account sensitive material remains external ref-only.",

items.title: PNC-010 storage ownership and PNC-019 runtime gating lack a machine-checkable handshake
items.statement: The row is owned by PNC-010 but declared blocked by PNC-019. Runtime enablement and policy refs are optional and nullable, with no required policy version, compatibility range, activation receipt, revocation state, or binding to contract_mode/runtime_adapter. The cross-document gate exists only as prose in this window.
items.impact: A consumer can interpret runtime enablement inconsistently or activate against an incompatible/stale lifecycle policy.
items.builder_discretion: Define a versioned activation/revocation handshake and conditional bindings among mode, adapter, policy snapshot, and enablement receipt.

evidence.exact_quote: "legacy_canonical_crosswalk_status": "Canonical Tier 0C-2 PlanCompileRun storage contract, still blocked by PNC-019 runtime lifecycle.",

items.title: Closed top-level objects and fixed schema identities constrain structural drift
items.statement: Both value schemas reject unspecified top-level properties and pin schema identifiers and versions with const values. This is an explicit structural safeguard even though several admitted nested values remain open.

items.title: Runtime-disabled bootstrap modes are explicitly enumerated
items.statement: The contract does not silently imply product-runtime availability: it fixes contract modes and the adapter to bootstrap-only/runtime-disabled values and says stale or unsupported runs remain disabled. This is a clear negative constraint at the enumerated-value level.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Resume by exact run id; stale currentness, unsupported contract mode, or missing receipts keep PlanCompile disabled.",

items.title: Narrative contracts explicitly prohibit embedded secrets
items.statement: Both families explicitly say sensitive provider/account material, transcripts, and credentials are excluded or external-ref-only. This is a stated privacy boundary, although GAP-004 and GAP-007 identify missing schema-level enforcement.

evidence.exact_quote: "redaction_no_secret_rule": "Stores ids, refs, hashes, stages, and enum status only; provider/account sensitive material remains external ref-only.",
"redaction_no_secret_rule": "Wave rows store document/PlanUnit refs and write boundaries only, never provider transcripts or credentials.",

dimension_assessments.summary: Operational consumers for migration, compaction, security/evidence verification, and support are not assigned.
Run status and wave status admit contradictory cross-field combinations and lack legal transition graphs.
No revision, CAS, lease, or idempotency identity protects resume, retry, or parent writeback.
Evidence resolution, retries, completion, and parent writeback have no coherent partial-failure protocol.
Cancellation, supersession, retry, resume, and ref revalidation do not define rollback boundaries or recovery ordering.
Key/value actor authority is unbound and wave resource boundaries are not mathematically enforceable.
A no-secret intent exists, but opaque fields and indefinite retention lack enforceable privacy and deletion controls.
Identifiers, refs, authority sets, opaque objects, and arrays lack canonical grammars and resource bounds.
The disabled-state consumer can receive contradictory readiness fields and lacks stable user-facing reason semantics.
External refs and receipts have no degraded/offline resolution state or safe revalidation protocol.
Opaque objects, evidence arrays, and authority sets have no byte, count, depth, or string-length limits.
The GUI projection lacks stable semantic reasons and change metadata from which accessible announcements and affordances can be derived.
Free-form blocker strings provide no locale-independent code and structured interpolation parameters.
Legacy non-buildable lineage and the PNC-019 activation boundary are not represented by versioned enforceable stored state.
Untyped refs and absent error/attempt metadata prevent reliable diagnosis, while no support consumer owns the lifecycle.
Cancellation and supersession do not require actor proof, reason, acknowledgement, propagation, or rollback metadata.
Operational ownership is missing and the PNC-010 to PNC-019 lifecycle gate is prose-only in the stored contract.
Opaque values and absent cross-field/set predicates prevent deterministic negative and transition oracles.
Open nested objects and an unversioned external runtime handshake create extension surfaces whose semantics cannot be bounded from this contract.
